Senior Engineering Director · Microsoft

Basharat Wani بشارت وانی

Basharat Wani is a builder. As a Senior Engineering Director at Microsoft in the CISO security organization, based in the Seattle area, he builds and protects Microsoft's Crown Jewels — working across security, red team and blue team, and sovereign cloud. It is the same work he has done at every stop: building the software engineering platforms underneath the products the world runs on, with a startup mindset — small teams, new services, and a bias for shipping.

At AWS, that mindset built new services at cloud scale. His One-Click Datacenter Resources Allocation Service lifted allocation accuracy from 23% to 64% across ~800 data centers, and with his team he launched the equipment master service as a new AWS service in six weeks. He moved 62 of 71 pipelines to CI/CD and cut tickets from 200+ to 25 a week — platform discipline that lets a service grow without breaking.

He learned the playbook at Rackspace, where he led the Cloud Apps portfolio — Email and Apps — from $22M to $70M in revenue, and grew engineering headcount from 22 to 140 people. He has scaled software engineering organizations multiple times, from 2 people to more than 100, and hired them himself — more than 800 interviews, choosing top engineering talent with care. His teams run on empowerment, psychological safety, and operational excellence, and the record is one of impactful delivery and accelerated promotions. The part of the story he tells most honestly is the failure: he is a multiple-time failed entrepreneur, and he treats those ventures as the education that made him a better leader — they taught him what scale actually costs, why hiring well matters, and why people must be safe to say what's failing before it fails loudly. That is why psychological safety isn't a slogan in his teams — it's the operating system. He keeps learning, keeps driving diversity and inclusion across the organizations he leads, and keeps his focus where the industry is heading: customer-centric approaches, digital transformation, distributed systems, data, and AI/ML platforms. Home is Bothell, Washington. He is a boomerang back into Microsoft. He also invests in early-stage startups — through angel investor networks and a small fund he helps manage — backing builders at the very beginning.

01

Career

Redmond, Washington

Microsoft

Microsoft — Senior Engineering Director, CISO Security Organization

Basharat's current role is Senior Engineering Director at Microsoft, based in the Seattle area. He works in Microsoft's CISO security organization, where his work centers on building and protecting Microsoft's Crown Jewels — the company's most critical assets.

In this role he is building and securing mission-critical workloads at scale, expanding Microsoft Security and GovCloud software and infrastructure.

This role is a boomerang back to Microsoft — Basharat worked at Microsoft earlier in his career and has now returned. It is the latest chapter of a career spent building and leading the platform and cloud systems that sit underneath products used at scale.

Redmond, Washington

Microsoft

Microsoft — Principal Software Group Engineering Manager

In his earlier stint at Microsoft, Basharat was Principal Software Group Engineering Manager. He led digital transformation with a focus on customers, driving software automation around Microsoft's corporate infrastructure using Azure Stack to support 180K global users, and partnered with customers, product managers, SLT and engineers to influence product strategy and roadmaps for Intelligent Infrastructure investments aligned with Microsoft's “Cloud First” mission. He developed and implemented a 4-Point-Go-Forward Strategy, gaining leadership buy-in.

He started as an individual contributor, then built and scaled 6 software engineering teams, ramping them to 37 engineers within 18 months.

  • Led the design, development and production rollout of a Network Device Code Upgrade Service, saving ~10K recurring engineering hours annually.
  • Led, designed and built the Microsoft Labs Asset Decommissioning Service, integrated with the Azure Circular Economy program, saving Microsoft $12 million annually in new hardware spending and reducing carbon emissions by 119 MTCO2.
  • Designed and built the Defrag Recommendation Service for Microsoft Lab Deployment, reducing cycle time from 2 months to 2 weeks for ~40 monthly deployments.
  • As part of a v-team, drove the AI/ML transformation journey across a 1200-person organization — wrote, partnered, and published multiple white papers and FAQ-PRs, contributed 30% of AI/ML opportunities, and shared a draft of the Copilot, LLM, and NLP platform.
  • Led, partnered, designed and built Computer Vision POCs for automating physical asset cycle count in Microsoft Labs.
  • Coached and mentored 40 individuals — engineers, software managers, program managers, and product managers.
  • Received multiple Beacon, Luminary, and NNIGN awards and achieved promotion.

He also experienced challenges in balancing innovation and engineering excellence and finding the right equilibrium between feature releases and reliability, leading to some failures.

Amazon Web Services

AWS / Amazon

Amazon Web Services — Senior Engineering Leader at AWS

At AWS / Amazon, where Basharat was a Senior Engineering Leader at AWS, he worked backwards from the customer promise — infinite cloud resources, on demand. That was customer obsession in practice: starting with what capacity planners and service teams actually needed, defining the vision and a three-year roadmap with them, and only then building.

That approach led to two new services. The One-Click Datacenter Resources Allocation Service lifted allocation accuracy from 23% to 64% across ~800 data centers. And with the team, he launched the equipment master service — a single source of truth for all data center equipment data — as a new AWS service in six weeks.

He moved fast, but deliberately — to balance innovation with reliability. He tested in small slices, failed early and failed fast when an idea didn't hold up, and kept the bar high where it mattered most: reliability. Innovation couldn't come at the cost of the capacity the cloud runs on — so the team automated relentlessly, moved 62 of 71 pipelines to CI/CD, and cut tickets from 200+ a week to 25.

As the org grew, he doubled the team multiple times across geographies — coaching engineers, TPMs, PMs, and managers so their growth tracked the business's biggest work.

Ascensus Inc.

Ascensus Inc.

Ascensus — VP Software Engineering

At Ascensus, Basharat was VP Software Engineering. He drove the Software Engineering and DevOps transformation journey in the organization from a service mindset, and evangelized, led, built, partnered, and successfully executed the vision of “Build and Deploy to production in hours” in the software engineering org, driving business and operational efficiency.

He led, coached, and supported the engineering organization in scaling from 30 software releases to 460 releases per year within 18 months, and grew the software engineering team from 90 to 240 engineers.

He led and fostered a culture of engineering excellence, emphasizing clean and secure code, blameless root cause analysis, monitoring, logging, analytics, metrics, HA, code refactoring, the IaaS to PaaS transition, blue-green deploys, agility, code ownership, and automation — and coached and mentored engineers, cultivating a culture of growth mindset, continuous learning and providing a psychological safety net.

Blacksburg, Virginia

Rackspace

Rackspace — Director of Software Development (Cloud Apps) · Head Product Development (Cloud Apps) · Senior Software Development Manager, Cloud Apps (R&D)

Basharat was Director of Software Development (Cloud Apps) at Rackspace. He started as a Software Development Manager and earned multiple promotions — including Senior Software Development Manager, Cloud Apps (R&D) and Head Product Development (Cloud Apps).

He led the Cloud Apps business — which grew from $22M to $70M in revenue, managing $18M in annual expenses and reporting to the SVP — and led, managed and shipped 8 major customer product releases for the Cloud Apps platform, expanding the engineering organization from 12 to 142 people.

He led software development at Rackspace's Blacksburg, Virginia location, a site of roughly 80 engineers. He is best documented there as a champion of the internal hackathon: the Blacksburg facility ran a 24-hour hackathon about every six months, with around half the engineering staff taking part — and, unusually, outsiders were welcome to join in.

  • Credited the program with solutions, new technologies, and proofs of concept that made it back into real work — and with a more engaged, more productive engineering culture.

Documented in Computerworld's feature “Hackathons for the rest of us” — see In Print below.

Credited 2014ZeniMax Online Studios

Director of Platform Engineering

ZeniMax Online Studios — The Elder Scrolls Online

In the official credits of The Elder Scrolls Online — the massively multiplayer online role-playing game developed by ZeniMax Online Studios and published by Bethesda Softworks — Basharat Wani is credited as Director of Platform Engineering, leading the Platform group alongside James Whitehouse, Director of Platform Services.

  • Platform leadership for one of the largest MMO launches of its era — a game built on ZeniMax's Megaserver technology, designed to hold players in one connected world without shard selection.
  • The game launched for PC and Mac on April 4, 2014, set roughly a thousand years before The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, with console versions following.

Credit as published in the game's credits, via the UESP Wiki and IGDB — see The Credit below.

02

In Print

Computerworld · Feature

“Hackathons for the rest of us”

Computerworld's survey of how companies build hackathons into their culture quotes Basharat throughout as the voice of Rackspace's Blacksburg site — on why engineers need room to build the ideas that sit behind the day job, what different formats actually produce, and why the whole thing only works if it stays cultural rather than official. Four of his lines from the piece:

They work 8 to 5 on their assignments backlog, but in the back of their heads they have great ideas that they never have time to work on.

— Basharat Wani, Director of Software Development, Rackspace (Blacksburg, Va.)

A note on the record. This page was compiled on October 30, 2026 from publicly available sources, linked above; his Bothell base and his X handle are his own current details. Basharat keeps a low public profile, so the documented record is deliberately short. It is also a common name: search results turn up a cricketer in Kashmir, designers and freelancers overseas, and an academic in Srinagar, among others. None of those are him — only the records matching his U.S. technology career — Microsoft, AWS / Amazon, Ascensus, Rackspace, and ZeniMax Online Studios — are included here, and records belonging to other people who share his name were excluded. The ZeniMax Online Studios credit is his own experience, and it stays on this page.
